hint_step_1: Remember that a class is a blueprint. What do we call an instance created from that blueprint?
hint_step_2: Look closely at the syntax used to instantiate a class in Python.
hint_step_3: Check if you forgot to use parentheses () when creating the object.

hint_step_1: Think about what creates an object. Does declaring a variable create it or does new?
hint_step_2: The new keyword tells Java to allocate memory for the object.
hint_step_3: A class defines the type; new creates the actual object.

hint_step_1: What is the difference between Student s; and Student s = new Student();?
hint_step_2: The first is just a reference
hint_step_3: the second creates an object.
column6: A declaration without new is just a null reference.

hint_step_1: What keyword prevents direct access to a field?
hint_step_2: Private restricts access to the declaring class.
hint_step_3: Private fields can only be accessed through methods of the same class.

hint_step_1: If a field is private
hint_step_2: how can other code read or change its value?
hint_step_3: Use getter and setter methods.
column6: Getters expose read access; setters validate changes before assignment.

hint_step_1: Why is it bad to make all fields public?
hint_step_2: Public fields allow uncontrolled mutation and break encapsulation.
hint_step_3: Encapsulation protects object invariants through controlled access.

hint_step_1: Which keyword declares that a class inherits from another?
hint_step_2: extends creates the parent-child relationship.
hint_step_3: A subclass uses extends to inherit accessible behavior from a superclass.

hint_step_1: Can a subclass access private fields of its parent?
hint_step_2: No
hint_step_3: private fields are not directly accessible to subclasses.
column6: Subclasses inherit behavior but access it through protected or public methods.

hint_step_1: When should you use composition instead of inheritance?
hint_step_2: Use composition when the relationship is has-a
hint_step_3: not is-a.
column6: Composition avoids the fragility of deep inheritance hierarchies.

hint_step_1: What must differ between two methods with the same name to be overloaded?
hint_step_2: The parameter list must differ in number or type.
hint_step_3: Return type alone is not enough for method overloading.

hint_step_1: Can you overload a method by changing only the return type?
hint_step_2: No
hint_step_3: Java distinguishes methods by signature not return type.
column6: The compiler needs distinct parameter lists to resolve overloaded calls.

hint_step_1: What determines which overloaded method is called?
hint_step_2: The argument types at compile time determine the match.
hint_step_3: Java resolves overloaded methods using the compile-time type of arguments.

hint_step_1: Which annotation marks a method that overrides a parent method?
hint_step_2: @Override tells the compiler to verify the override.
hint_step_3: The annotation ensures the method signature matches the parent.

hint_step_1: If Parent p = new Child(); and both have speak()
hint_step_2: which version runs?
hint_step_3: The Child version runs due to runtime dispatch.
column6: Overriding means the actual object type determines which method runs.

hint_step_1: Can you override a method by changing only the parameter list?
hint_step_2: No
hint_step_3: that is overloading. Overriding requires the same signature.
column6: Overriding replaces the parent method with a compatible signature.

hint_step_1: Why does overriding support polymorphism?
hint_step_2: It allows a parent reference to call a subclass method at runtime.
hint_step_3: Polymorphism depends on overriding to enable different runtime behavior.

hint_step_1: What is the difference between method overloading and method overriding?
hint_step_2: Overloading is compile-time same-class; overriding is runtime parent-child.
hint_step_3: Overloading uses different parameters; overriding uses the same signature in a subclass.

hint_step_1: If Animal a = new Dog(); and a.sound() calls Dog.sound()
hint_step_2: what is this called?
hint_step_3: Dynamic dispatch or runtime polymorphism.
column6: The JVM selects the method based on the actual object type

hint_step_1: Can polymorphism exist without inheritance and overriding?
hint_step_2: No
hint_step_3: polymorphism requires a common type and overridden behavior.
column6: Polymorphism is the runtime effect enabled by inheritance and overriding.

hint_step_1: What happens when a parent reference points to a child object?
hint_step_2: The child overrides methods called through that reference.
hint_step_3: This is the core of runtime polymorphism in Java.

hint_step_1: What is a constructor and what is its purpose?
hint_step_2: A constructor initializes object state when Java creates an instance.
hint_step_3: Constructors have the same name as the class and no return type.

hint_step_1: What is the purpose of a getter method?
hint_step_2: A getter exposes read access to a private field.
hint_step_3: Getters return the value without allowing external mutation.

hint_step_1: What is the difference between extends and implements?
hint_step_2: extends is for class inheritance
hint_step_3: implements is for interfaces.
column6: A class uses extends for a parent class relationship.

hint_step_1: Can two methods have the same name and same parameters but different return types?
hint_step_2: No
hint_step_3: Java does not allow overloading by return type alone.
column6: The parameter list must differ to create a distinct overloaded method.

hint_step_1: What is the role of super() in method overriding?
hint_step_2: super() calls the parent method from the subclass.
hint_step_3: super() allows a subclass to invoke the overridden parent version.

hint_step_1: Does the variable type or the object type determine which overridden method runs?
hint_step_2: The actual object type determines runtime behavior.
hint_step_3: This is the fundamental mechanism behind polymorphism.
